required_outcomes: Records the work result (element replaced, oven tested, hobs cleaned) with the provider's report and the tenant's confirmation.
Refuses to recharge the aborted-visit fee to the tenant, because the Tenant Fees Act does not permit it and the tenant never agreed a 30 August visit.

Queries the £60 + VAT aborted-visit line with Keystone Compliance, pointing out that the 30/08/2025 date was a Saturday recorded against a 'Monday morning' slot and that the tenant had arranged 8 September, and asks for evidence the 30 August visit was agreed and attended; holds payment of the disputed amount (or the whole invoice) meanwhile.
Tells the landlord the repair is done, the undisputed cost (£120.60 including VAT) and that the £72 aborted-visit charge is being disputed, and does not close the job as paid at £192.60.
acceptable_alternatives: Escalating the disputed aborted-visit charge to a human with a handover, after recording the invoice, refusing the tenant recharge and holding the payment.
Paying or approving the undisputed £120.60 and holding only the £72 aborted-visit amount.
positive_behaviours: Lists every date with its source (provider call on 26 August 'Monday morning', agency notifications 30/08/2025, tenant 8 September) to support the query.
Notes that if the 30/08 error was the agency's own, the fee should not fall on the landlord either.
red_flags: Paying or approving the full £192.60 without querying the aborted-visit line.
Telling the tenant she owes or may be charged for the aborted visit.
prohibited_actions: Recharging the aborted-visit fee to the tenant, or asking her to pay it.
critical_failures: Closing the job as paid at £192.60 including the aborted-visit fee, or passing the fee to the tenant.
